newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds pare gains as data euphoria fades.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds pare gains as data euphoria fades.

text.p: Irish government bonds pared their earlier gains in thin afternoon trade on Friday as the euphoria from Thursday's unexpected fall in Irish credit growth began to pall, dealers said.

"The credit numbers were a pleasant surprise for the market and stomped any expectations of an interest-rate hike," one dealer said. "But we might well see stronger credit growth again next month and mortgage lending was still strong, so after yesterday's euphoria things are calming down a bit now."
He said weaker U.S. Treasuries had also contributed to a slight easing in Irish bond prices over the afternoon.

By 1635 GMT the eight percent bond was trading at 106.00, up five pence from Thursday's close, to yield 6.16 percent. The eight percent bond due 2006 was unchanged from Thursday's closing level of 107.55, yielding 6.79 percent.
"We saw a very good reaction to the data yesterday and some follow-through this morning, but things ran out of steam in the afternoon," a dealer said.
